text.content:
Every character has a Nature (the true self, shaped by upbringing and changed only rarely by extraordinary events) and a Demeanor (the public mask, which can shift freely). Both are chosen from the same list of Archetypes, and a character's Nature and Demeanor may be identical, though few Kindred are so transparent. Archetypes also govern when a character regains spent Willpower through good roleplaying.

The Archetypes

  • Architect: Builds lasting works or institutions, thinking in terms of legacies and grand designs.
  • Autocrat: Needs to be in charge and expects obedience from those around her.
  • Bon Vivant: Lives for pleasure and sensation, savoring every indulgence unlife offers.
  • Bravo: Solves problems through intimidation and force, reveling in confrontation.
  • Caregiver: Finds purpose in protecting and nurturing others, even at personal cost.
  • Celebrant: Lives for revelry, ritual, or chaos, throwing herself fully into the moment.
  • Child: Relies on others for guidance and protection, reacting to the world with innocence or petulance.
  • Competitor: Measures self-worth by besting others, turning everything into a contest.
  • Conformist: Finds security in fitting in and following the group's lead.
  • Conniver: Achieves goals through manipulation, deception, and angling for advantage.
  • Curmudgeon: Meets the world with cynicism and complaint, expecting the worst of everyone.
  • Deviant: Defines herself by rejecting norms and expectations, often deliberately shocking others.
  • Director: Organizes and commands situations, most comfortable when running the show.
  • Fanatic: Pursues a cause or belief with single-minded, often dangerous devotion.
  • Gallant: Charms and impresses others, thriving on admiration and romance.
  • Judge: Seeks fairness and balance, weighing situations and rendering verdicts.
  • Loner: Prefers self-reliance and isolation, uneasy relying on or trusting others.
  • Martyr: Sacrifices for others, sometimes seeking out suffering as proof of devotion.
  • Masochist: Finds meaning, relief, or pleasure through pain and hardship.
  • Monster: Embraces cruelty or predation as her true nature, with little pretense of restraint.
  • Pedagogue: Teaches and mentors others, defining herself through passing on knowledge.
  • Penitent: Driven by guilt, seeking atonement for real or perceived sins.
  • Perfectionist: Holds herself and others to exacting standards, intolerant of failure.
  • Rebel: Resists authority and convention on principle, valuing defiance for its own sake.
  • Rogue: Acts purely out of self-interest, unpredictable and difficult to pin down.
  • Survivor: Focused above all on enduring, adapting to whatever threatens her continued existence.
  • Thrill-Seeker: Craves excitement and novelty, growing restless without risk or adventure.
  • Traditionalist: Values established order, ritual, and the old ways above innovation.
  • Trickster: Delights in deception, pranks, and upending expectations for amusement.
  • Visionary: Driven by a grand idea or dream of the future, often at odds with present reality.
